title: Switch Transformers: Scaling to Trillion Parameter Models with Simple and Efficient Sparsity
authors: William Fedus, Barret Zoph, Noam Shazeer
date: January 2021 (arXiv v1 11 January 2021; JMLR 2022; arXiv v3 June 2022)

code.title: google-research/t5x
code.note: JAX code and all model checkpoints (repo, about 20 minutes for the README and entry path); the model configurations live in flaxformer's t5x/configs/moe/models/switch_*.gin, which this page uses to settle two Table 9 rows

live.text: train a Switch layer in your browser

takeaway: Simplified MoE to top-1 routing with a single balancing loss and selective fp32, getting 7x faster pretraining than T5-Base at equal FLOPs and the first 1.6T-parameter model.

headline.k: Switch-Base, 64 experts, to T5-Base's quality, same 32 TPUv3 cores and FLOPs per token
headline.d: 7.5x on a step basis; read off curves, no table

headline.k: to a fixed quality at capacity factor 1.0, against 80.1 for top-2 MoE
Switch-C: 2,048 experts in every FFN, trained with no instability
headline.d: recounted from its configuration to within 0.1%

resources.n: the canonical MoE explainer; its sections on Switch routing, capacity factor, load balancing and selective precision are essentially a modern restatement of this paper.

resources.t: A Visual Guide to Mixture of Experts
resources.n: the clearest diagrams of the router, expert capacity and token dropping; walks through the Switch simplification step by step.
places Switch in the lineage from Shazeer 2017 and GShard through Mixtral and DeepSeekMoE, with the sparse against active parameter arithmetic.
an hour-long read-through of the paper with commentary on the routing and scaling claims.
the reference implementation the paper's Code Blocks 14 to 16 are abridged from: the router, the capacity mask and the dispatch and combine tensors.

resources.t: ST-MoE: Designing Stable and Transferable Sparse Expert Models
resources.by: Zoph, Bello, Kumar, Du, Huang, Dean, Shazeer, Fedus, 2022
resources.n: the same group's sequel: the router z-loss, why bfloat16 breaks the router softmax (with a worked example this page reproduces), and the revision of top-1 to top-2 routing.

kb.n: 2017: the Transformer whose feed-forward sub-block the Switch layer replaces.
2019: the dense baseline, the C4 corpus and the span-corruption objective every Switch model is measured with.

kb.t: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
kb.n: 2020: the dense scaling results Switch extends with a fourth axis, parameters at fixed FLOPs; also the FLOP-counting convention of the paper's footnote 7.
2019: tensor model parallelism, the technique Switch combines with expert and data parallelism in §5.
2019: the other route to trillion parameters, sharding optimiser state of a dense model instead of adding sparse experts.
2024: the open-weights descendant that made the sparse FFN template mainstream; top-2 where Switch is top-1, no capacity machinery on GPUs.
2024: modern high-sparsity MoE; its auxiliary-loss-free balancing answers the balance against quality tension of the loss introduced here.

kb.t: Bounding the memory bottlenecks of large mixture-of-experts training
kb.n: 2026: bounds the four memory bottlenecks of large-MoE training (expert dispatch, vocabulary projection, activation checkpointing, optimiser state) by scheduling rather than approximation; its row is summarised from an abstract only.

topics.t: Topic: llms, Deeper: inside an MoE tab
topics.n: the generic MoE layer this page does not rebuild: softmax against sigmoid routers, top-k styles, a capacity and dropping animation, global-batch balancing, expert parallelism and configs of current MoE models.
the fine-grained, shared-expert and bias-balanced end of the lineage, with its expert placement and EPLB.

verdict: Believe the engineering: one expert per token, one balancing loss, a float32 router and a smaller initialisation made sparse training cheap and stable enough to reach 1.57T parameters, and the balancing loss and float32 router are still in today's configurations. Treat the size of the speedups (7x, 4x) as single runs read off curves, and the top-1 over top-2 margin as within noise: the same group recommended top-2 a year later.
